doc.body:
:obj:`LibTmux.Server <LibTmux.Server>` documents ownership and failure recovery. Typed IDs,
 checked dimensions and supported releases have their own pure modules.
doc.summary:
Capture tmux state in IO and process detached observations with ordinary
 Haskell collections. Start with :obj:`withServer <LibTmux.Server#v:withServer>` and :obj:`capture <LibTmux.Server#v:capture>`; navigation and
 field access from :obj:`LibTmux.Snapshot <LibTmux.Snapshot>` perform no external operations.

doc.body:
Parsing and rendering are pure. An ID carries no endpoint, server lifetime
 or liveness evidence. Render an ID for external text; use its numeric
 accessor when an application needs the mathematical value.

Start with :obj:`parseSessionId <LibTmux.Id#v:parseSessionId>`, :obj:`parseWindowId <LibTmux.Id#v:parseWindowId>` or :obj:`parsePaneId <LibTmux.Id#v:parsePaneId>`. Each type's
 documentation links its parser and renderer. Contextual numeric indices
 belong to :obj:`LibTmux.Value <LibTmux.Value>`.



```haskell
>>> :set -XOverloadedStrings
>>> fmap renderWindowId (parseWindowId "@17")
Right "@17"
>>> either (const "rejected") renderPaneId (parsePaneId "@17")
"rejected"
```
doc.summary: Distinct session, physical-window and physical-pane IDs.

doc.body:
A :obj:`Server <LibTmux.Server#t:Server>` represents one adoption of one endpoint. :obj:`withServer <LibTmux.Server#v:withServer>` owns its
 socket pin, native command clients and cleanup workers. Closing this scope
 releases those resources; it does not send `kill-server`. The tmux noun
 `Client` refers to detached observations in :obj:`LibTmux.Snapshot <LibTmux.Snapshot>`.
 :obj:`withRuntime <LibTmux.Server#v:withRuntime>` and :obj:`withServerIn <LibTmux.Server#v:withServerIn>` give several handles shared resource limits
 and independent Server scopes.

:obj:`capture <LibTmux.Server#v:capture>` returns fully decoded, validated values. Field access and graph
 navigation are pure. Captures use an observation interval, not an atomic
 transaction over tmux and operating-system state.

Operational failures use :obj:`TmuxException <LibTmux.Server#t:TmuxException>`. :obj:`tryTmux <LibTmux.Server#v:tryTmux>` catches that type only.
 Cancellation retains its original exception class. If bounded cleanup
 cannot finish, :obj:`cleanupRecoveries <LibTmux.Server#v:cleanupRecoveries>` retrieves the owning recovery scope
 from the exception context. A failed callback remains the primary failure.
doc.summary: Observe an existing tmux daemon through an owned Server handle.

doc.body:
:obj:`LibTmux.Server <LibTmux.Server>` acquires a :obj:`Snapshot <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:Snapshot>` in IO. Every operation in this
 module reads owned Haskell values, including after the Server closes.
 Use ordinary lists, comprehensions and folds for application predicates.

:obj:`Window <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:Window>` and :obj:`Pane <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:Pane>` are physical entities. A :obj:`WindowLink <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:WindowLink>` identifies an
 observed session*index*window binding; :obj:`PaneOccurrence <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:PaneOccurrence>` retains that
 context. :obj:`paneOccurrences <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:paneOccurrences>` therefore preserves repeated appearances while
 :obj:`panes <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:panes>` lists each physical pane once.

References compare identity within one Server generation. A lookup reads
 the supplied snapshot, including a newer snapshot from that same Server.
 Independent Server scopes have different generations. Resolve an ID again
 with :obj:`lookupPaneId <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:lookupPaneId>` when deliberately selecting a newly observed entity.

Observation fields are exported for record dot and local updates. Editing
 a record does not change a snapshot's indexes or establish provenance.
 :obj:`LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture <LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture>` constructs validated offline snapshots;
 :obj:`snapshotOrigin <LibTmux.Snapshot#v:snapshotOrigin>` distinguishes them from observations acquired through IO.
doc.summary: Detached tmux observations and pure navigation.

doc.body:
No operation in this module contacts tmux. Named fixture references can
 model successive observations; they never equal a live Server generation.
 Snapshot and live-reference constructors remain hidden.
 Validation checks graph and metadata laws; wire decoding, tmux normalization
 and transport limits belong to acquisition rather than fixture construction.

Start with :obj:`fixtureOrigin <LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture#v:fixtureOrigin>` and :obj:`emptyFixture <LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture#v:emptyFixture>`, construct ordinary observation
 records using this module's reference builders, then call :obj:`validateFixture <LibTmux.Snapshot.Fixture#v:validateFixture>`.
doc.summary: Build validated detached snapshots for pure application tests.

doc.body:
Construction and access are pure. Window-link indices and pane indices
 have distinct types; neither substitutes for an entity ID. A constructor
 checks the mathematical domain, while command-specific limits belong at
 the operation boundary. Use :obj:`mkDimension <LibTmux.Value#v:mkDimension>`, :obj:`mkWindowIndex <LibTmux.Value#v:mkWindowIndex>` and :obj:`mkPaneIndex <LibTmux.Value#v:mkPaneIndex>`
 to validate input; their accessors return mathematical integers. Entity
 identifiers belong to :obj:`LibTmux.Id <LibTmux.Id>`.



```haskell
>>> fmap dimensionValue (mkDimension 120)
Right 120
>>> mkDimension 0
Left (NonPositiveDimension 0)
```
doc.summary: Positive dimensions and nonnegative contextual indices.

doc.body:
These functions consume supplied text. They neither execute `tmux -V`
 nor contact a server. Admission checks the inclusive 3.3a through 3.8 range;
 individual features still need capability and conformance checks.

Use :obj:`parseVersion <LibTmux.Version#v:parseVersion>` for input, :obj:`requireSupported <LibTmux.Version#v:requireSupported>` for supported-range
 admission and :obj:`renderVersion <LibTmux.Version#v:renderVersion>` for canonical output.



```haskell
>>> :set -XOverloadedStrings
>>> fmap renderVersion (parseVersion "tmux 3.3a\n" >>= requireSupported)
Right "3.3a"
```
doc.summary: Parse stable tmux releases and check the supported release range.

Open one handle, run the callback, then perform bounded owned cleanup.
 Cleanup never replaces a callback exception. Incomplete cleanup raises
 :obj:`CleanupFailed <LibTmux.Server#v:CleanupFailed>` after success, or annotates the original callback failure
 with a reachable :obj:`CleanupRecovery <LibTmux.Server#t:CleanupRecovery>`. No daemon shutdown is requested.

doc.summary:
Acquire the complete baseline graph, metadata and attached clients.
 Returned values own their data and remain usable after :obj:`withServer <LibTmux.Server#v:withServer>` exits.
 Capacity and acquisition failure are errors; they never become empty lists.
The handle's opaque generation, available without contacting tmux.

Shared resource limits and cleanup ownership for Server handles. Create
 one with :obj:`withRuntime <LibTmux.Server#v:withRuntime>`, then adopt endpoints through :obj:`withServerIn <LibTmux.Server#v:withServerIn>`.
 Detached :obj:`Snapshot <LibTmux.Snapshot#t:Snapshot>` values retain no Runtime.

Own a Runtime for the callback and perform bounded cleanup afterward.
 Closing it retires every adopted handle; application-owned threads remain
 the application's responsibility. Late adoption fails with :obj:`RuntimeClosed <LibTmux.Server#v:RuntimeClosed>`.
 The daemon remains running.

doc.body:
Failed adoption can retain a :obj:`CleanupRecovery <LibTmux.Server#t:CleanupRecovery>` before a :obj:`Server <LibTmux.Server#t:Server>` exists.
 Inspection, retry and waiting through that owner stay scoped to the failed
 adoption. Cleanup preserves application exceptions, incoming masking state
 and cancellation; known acquisition failures use :obj:`TmuxException <LibTmux.Server#t:TmuxException>`.
